best_narrative.headline: Zocdoc: Telehealth Competitors Mobilize NY Lobbying Amid Hims Litigation
best_narrative.body: Zocdoc operates a healthcare directory and marketplace connecting patients to providers across multiple service categories, creating exposure to state medical advertising and fee-splitting enforcement distinct from pure-play telehealth operators. Four competitors filed federal lobbying disclosures on telehealth policy between June and July 2026, signaling organized industry response to regulatory pressure. The May 2026 Hims and Hers litigation drew public attention to anti-kickback and consumer protection vulnerabilities in the telehealth distribution model. Operators in this segment commonly face New York state scrutiny on advertising claims, referral economics, and medical board jurisdictional boundaries.

Given Zocdoc's exposure as a multi-service healthcare marketplace in New York, your government affairs team should map how these enforcement precursors may reshape advertising and referral standards in your core markets. Prospect: We've been monitoring Hims, but we're not sure how much it applies to our marketplace model. BDR Pivot: That distinction is exactly why a 10-minute sync makes sense now. Your government affairs team needs to model whether the enforcement vectors opening up in Hims cases translate to your referral economics and state advertising rules. Can we grab 10 minutes next week to walk through what's different about your exposure?

best_narrative.headline: Spring Health: NY Mental Health Telehealth Competitor Lobbying Intensifies
best_narrative.body: Spring Health operates as a pure-play mental health platform embedded in employer-sponsored benefits with state behavioral health licensing exposure across top jurisdictions including New York. Two telehealth competitors filed federal lobbying disclosures in April 2026 on telehealth policy topics, signaling coordinated industry advocacy as regulatory scrutiny on asynchronous prescribing and reimbursement standards tightens. Industry-standard regulatory exposures for this business model include state-level Medicaid mental health carve-out restrictions, employer plan compliance amendments, and behavioral health licensing reciprocity challenges. The recent Hims and Hers litigation reinforces that enforcement momentum on telehealth clinical workflows now extends to mental health modalities, creating material exposure in New York and peer states.
